raw_result.summary: T006 cannot exercise authorization-only Web through a real public seam because the accepted definition does not name the host-mode selector/composition entrypoint or the controlled certificate-identity verification boundary. Guessing configuration or injecting test-only routes/authentication would bypass the behavior under test.

finding.evidence: Current Vulgata.Web Program unconditionally configures ordinary services, migrates ordinary Identity/domain stores, and maps the ordinary API. No October mode selector, bootstrap composition entrypoint, or existing certificate-auth test seam is present.
finding.required_outcome: Name an explicit closed Web startup mode selector and public composition boundary for Ordinary, OctoberAuthorizationOnly, and later OctoberSelectedData modes. Name a production certificate-identity verifier input that validates target-scoped allowlisting and can receive controlled certificate identity in SelfContained tests without weakening the real authentication boundary. Preserve ordinary startup, two-route bootstrap isolation, and the external certificate qualification gate.

preserved_work.verification: Foundational October filter passed 34/34, policy checks passed, and Infrastructure build had zero errors.

raw_result.test_discovery: T006 test owner made no edits. Existing Identity factory patterns can cover cookie and ManagementAccess behavior once the accepted mode and certificate seams are selectable.
raw_result.authority_effect: The affected implementation path returns to plan. Existing human approvals remain historical but require corrected-hash review and rebinding before production resumes. No external resource permission is inferred.
